dbe_source.recommendation: Teachers need to emphasise the importance of the sign of the middle term in factorising quadratic equations.

lesson.concept: In x² + bx + c = 0, the two factors are (x - r₁)(x - r₂) where b = -(r₁ + r₂) and c = r₁ · r₂. The sign of b and the sign of c together tell you the signs of the roots.
lesson.why: If c is positive, the roots have the same sign. If c is negative, the roots have opposite signs. Then b tells you which way each sign goes.

work: c = +10, so the two numbers have the same sign.
b = +7, so both numbers are positive.
Find two positive numbers that multiply to 10 and add to 7.

probe.hint: c = -10, so the two numbers have opposite signs. b = -3, so the larger magnitude carries the negative sign.

learner_message: The two numbers are close, but one sign is wrong. Check that the sum matches b and the product matches c.
